shots.label: rbih-campaign-opening
shots.text: WAR BEGINS: 6 APR 1992 × DATE 6 Apr 1992 The referendum has been held. Armed conflict is now inevitable. WHO YOU ARE IDENTITY You are the President of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, recognized by the world on 6 April and besieged the same day. You preside over a multi-ethnic state that half its own citizens have taken up arms to dismantle. SITUATION Recognition arrived; weapons did not. An international arms embargo binds your hands while the heights above Sarajevo, Tuzla, and the Drina belong to a former federal army that kept its tanks and its officers. Your defenders are territorial units, police, and volunteers — Bosniak, Serb, Croat — outnumbered in guns by an order of magnitude. You hold the cities and little of the ground between them. The killing in Zvornik and Bijeljina has already begun. WHAT YOU CANNOT ESCAPE You must defend a civic republic with a citizen army that the fighting is already turning into a single-nation force — and you have no guns to spare for the gap between what you believe and what you can hold. ARBIH YOU The Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina musters from territorial defense units, police, and volunteers. Poorly armed but defending homeland, its early survival depends on holding urban centers and buying time for organization. 78 brigades 48.7k pers 32 tanks 102 arty VRS The Army of Republika Srpska inherits JNA equipment, officers, and doctrine. Professional and heavily armed, the VRS holds a decisive early advantage but faces long-term attrition as reserves thin. 64 brigades Unreported pers Unreported tanks Unreported arty HVO The Croatian Defence Council organizes around western Herzegovina and central Bosnia enclaves. Capable but geographically fragmented, the HVO walks a tightrope between alliance with ARBiH and its own territorial ambitions. PRESIDENTIAL RESPONSE Civic multi-ethnic republic HISTORICAL DEFAULT This is the historically attested choice. You are free to choose any option. One republic, all citizens equal. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina morale +2 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Internal Cohesion +5 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Int'l Standing +5 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Negotiating Leverage -10 SITUATION Your Presidency must declare its vision for the state. The platform drafted in May declares a multi-ethnic, civic republic where all citizens are equal regardless of ethnicity. But the war is testing that ideal. shots.text: DIPLOMATIC INTERNATIONAL PEACE PROPOSAL Cutileiro Plan (Lisbon Agreement) Proposed: 6 Apr 1992 The EC-brokered Cutileiro Plan proposes dividing Bosnia-Herzegovina into three ethnically-defined cantons under a weak central government. Each constituent people would govern areas where they form a majority. The split would give Bosniaks and Serbs 44% each, with Croats receiving 12%. All three sides initially agreed in Lisbon, but the deal is fragile — rejection by any party will signal that partition cannot be achieved through negotiation alone. shots.text: DECISION REQUIRED Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina · 27 Apr 1992 Paramilitary Authorization Policy PRESIDENTIAL RESPONSE Refuse paramilitary deployment HISTORICAL DEFAULT This is the historically attested choice. You are free to choose any option. Single chain of command. Irregular formations are integrated into regular ARBiH regiments under Main Staff authority or refused entry to the order of battle. The Patriotic League cadres are absorbed; the Sarajevo-area independent brigades will be brought to heel. International monitors note the posture; the hardline current inside SDA bristles at the constraint. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Int'l Standing +5 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Internal Cohesion -3 Review each deployment Each proposed deployment arrives in the Presidency files with a casualty projection. Regional ARBiH commanders lose blanket authority; the political center retains the decision. Operational tempo slows; the integration line softens; the international monitors note the reviews but reserve judgment until the pattern emerges. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Int'l Standing -3 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Internal Cohesion -2 Authorize paramilitary standing orders Standing authorization. The Patriotic League cadres, the Sarajevo-area independent brigades, the volunteer detachments — all operate on local commander authority without per-mission political review. This breaks with the documented Sarajevo posture. International monitors will read the pattern against Pale and Mostar; the ICTY paper trail will record the policy in its own terms. Each approved sweep records civilian casualties and increments the war-crimes counter through the existing engine surface. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Int'l Standing -25 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Negotiating Leverage -15 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Internal Cohesion 0 SITUATION Sarajevo Presidency files. The Presidency posture toward integration is in question. The documented Sarajevo position, since the Patriotic League's absorption into ARBiH, has been a single chain

shots.text: EVENT × 1 of 2 HUMANITARIAN Foca The Takeover And Its Aftermath The historical record of the takeover of Foca, at the confluence of the Drina and Cehotina rivers, is documented here. Across the Krnojelac, Kunarac and Karadzic judgments, the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia established the conditions at the KP Dom detention facility and convicted, in the Kunarac case, for sexual enslavement and rape as crimes against humanity, establishing those legal categories in international criminal law. The pre-war Bosniak community of the municipality was reduced to a residual presence by the end of 1992. INTELLIGENCE ASSESSMENT The historical record of the Foca takeover is documented in the Codex.
